description: We are a team of enthusiastic school students passionate about science, technology, engineering, space exploration and innovation. Guided by our STEAM mentor at JBM Global School, we enjoy exploring new ideas, experimenting with technology and turning creative concepts into real-world projects.
summary: ASTRA-X is a browser-based 3D survival game that lets students feel what it is like to be an astronaut stranded on Mars. Players explore the planet, find fuel cells, collect resources, craft tools, repair and drive a rover, and survive dust storms and meteor strikes while managing oxygen, food, battery and health. Every device and discovery unlocks a short knowledge file that explains the science behind it, so students learn how real space technology works by playing, not by answering a quiz. It runs on phones and computers with no install.
details:
What it does and how it works. ASTRA-X is a browser-based 3D survival game that makes students feel like an astronaut stranded on Mars. The player explores the planet, finds three lost fuel cells, collects iron, ice, scrap and circuits, crafts tools, repairs and drives a rover, investigates a mysterious radio signal and returns to the lander. Oxygen, food, battery and health drain constantly, and dust storms and meteor strikes make survival harder. Every new item or device unlocks a short knowledge file explaining how it works, why it matters in space and its link to a real NASA mission. These files are collected in a Knowledge Database.

Benefits and intended impact. Students learn life support, power, robotics, resource use and radio communication by making survival decisions, not by memorising answers. It runs in any phone or computer browser with no install, so any school can use it. We hope it makes younger students curious about space careers.

Tools and technology. HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one web page, Three.js (WebGL) for 3D graphics and shadows, GitHub Pages for hosting, and an AI assistant to help write code. Terrain, rocks and textures are generated in code.

What is creative. It is a real playable game with exploration, crafting and a drivable rover, not a quiz. Learning is built into the mission, and students can customise their astronaut’s suit.

Factors we considered. Scientific accuracy (the facts are simplified and labelled as simplified), mobile controls for students without computers, student privacy (the optional face photo never leaves the browser) and keeping the game playable on ordinary devices.
